source_candidate.subject: OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks

official_repository.repository_status: placeholder only; README states source code and documentation are being prepared and will be released soon

findings.finding: The paper gives a coherent high-level release lifecycle, but the currently linked official repository does not yet release the implementation needed to reproduce that lifecycle.
evidence: The paper explicitly separates evidence, candidate generation, paired candidate validation, release, subsequent-task activation, monitoring and rollback.
The official GitHub repository root contains only README.md at audited head 66dd3fe9.
That README explicitly says source code and documentation are being prepared and will be released soon.
findings.scope_correction: Treat the paper's repository link as an announced official code location, not as currently available official implementation support.

findings.finding: Champion-Challenger pairing is specified, but concrete gate thresholds are not recoverable from the paper alone.
evidence: The method defines Gate(P, Theta) across benefit, evidence quality, tail risk and resource-cost constraints.
The paper states possible statistics such as pair count, win rate, confidence interval, task failures and tail losses, but does not publish the concrete numeric Theta used for the reported runs.
The online algorithm accepts Trig and CanaryMonitor as abstract operators.
findings.scope_correction: The governance architecture is specified; the exact release decision rule used in the headline experiment is not exactly replayable from the public paper/repository state.

findings.finding: Online trigger and post-release rollback are described semantically, but their operational thresholds are unspecified in the currently public materials.
evidence: The paper says Trig may depend on feedback amount, update period or task stage.
It says CanaryMonitor rolls back when a degradation condition is met and quarantines triggering traces.
No numeric trigger schedule or degradation threshold is stated in the paper, and no implementation/config is available in the official repo to resolve it.
findings.scope_correction: Do not claim that a particular trigger or rollback threshold has been independently validated; the reported YC-Bench result evaluates the bundled OLE configuration as a whole.

findings.finding: The primary YC-Bench result is positive but remains a small, single-benchmark primary-study result without a protocol-matched independent rerun located in this audit.
evidence: With deepseek-v4-flash, official medium setting, seeds 1/2/3 and 20-turn context, Table II reports fixed-pi0 73.89% task success and 365,976.30 mean final funds; OLE-online 87.87% and 878,601.79; OLE-offline 91.80% and 974,627.52.
Annual survival is 1/3, 2/3 and 3/3 respectively for fixed-pi0, online and offline.
The paper identifies broader cross-scenario validity and evolution stability as future work.
findings.scope: Supports the exact reported YC-Bench configuration as primary-study evidence, not general long-horizon superiority.

findings.finding: The published token totals undercount all-in evolution cost because candidate-generation token usage was not retained.
evidence: Table III reports OLE-online 34.70M main-task + 29.82M evolution-validation = 64.52M observable tokens, and OLE-offline 35.61M + 24.02M = 59.63M.
The paper explicitly states these totals exclude candidate-generation calls whose usage was not retained.
findings.scope_correction: 64.52M and 59.63M are observable lower bounds for the counted categories, not complete all-in token costs of evolution.

findings.finding: The located independent auto-research implementation is a declared deterministic L1 mini-suite, not a reproduction of OLE's YC-Bench release/rollback lifecycle.
evidence: Its OpenLoopEvolveAgent subclasses a generic ExactMechanismAgent whose solve() returns the task's supplied answer and plan.

The OLE-specific implementation increments diagnostic counters for planning, verifier calls, archival writes and periodic refinements; it does not implement actual candidate generation, paired gate thresholds, version activation, CanaryMonitor rollback or YC-Bench.
Its saved metric labels fidelity as mechanism reproduction on deterministic benchmark mini-suites, uses only seed 42, marks formal_comparison=false and warns not to claim a stable improvement.
Its provenance says dataset fingerprint and original code commit were not recorded in the historical artifact.
findings.scope_correction: Count this as an independent synthetic interface/mechanism emulation only. It does not independently reproduce the paper's headline results or the claimed robust release semantics.

findings.finding: No component ablation located here isolates the causal contribution of release gating, trigger choice, or rollback monitoring from the rest of OLE.
evidence: The reported experiment compares Native, fixed initial policy, OLE-online and OLE-offline fixed policy.
The paper reports 12 online candidate-update attempts and offline candidate search settings, but no matched gate-off/rollback-off/trigger-threshold ablation table was identified.
findings.scope_correction: The experiment supports the bundled OLE configurations; it does not establish that any one governance component is independently responsible for the observed gains.

published_claims_checked.yc_bench: Primary-study Table II values are internally recoverable from the paper and support a strong bundled-config improvement under the stated three-seed YC-Bench setup.
published_claims_checked.offline_search: Paper states k=3 candidates with a preregistered maximum of 4 candidate rounds for offline evolution.
published_claims_checked.release_and_rollback: Architecture is explicit, but exact operational gate/trigger/rollback parameters are not publicly replayable from current materials.
published_claims_checked.token_cost: Published totals are observable counted costs and explicitly exclude unretained candidate-generation calls.

independent_reproduction_search.partial_result: daiwk/auto-research provides a one-seed deterministic planbench-mini mechanism adapter and explicitly disclaims full external-environment reproduction.

reproduction_blockers: Official source code and documentation are not released in the linked repository at the audited head.

No public exact run bundle binding the headline cells to implementation commit, Loop Policy assets, candidate prompts, gate thresholds, trigger configuration, Canary degradation threshold, model endpoint/version, raw trajectories and per-seed outputs was located.
Candidate-generation token usage was not retained, preventing complete all-in cost reconstruction from the paper's token tables.
No protocol-matched independent YC-Bench rerun was located.
The located independent mini-suite intentionally omits the full external environment and core release/rollback lifecycle.
reopen_conditions: The authors publish substantive official source/configuration at yoyoshikc/OpenLoopEvolve.
A paper-authored raw run bundle appears with exact gate/trigger/rollback parameters and per-seed trajectories.
A protocol-matched independent YC-Bench rerun appears.
A matched component ablation isolates Gate, Trig, CanaryMonitor or rollback effects under fixed model/tasks/seeds/budget.
